newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Autoliv says new group eyeing fresh market.
newsitem.headline: Autoliv says new group eyeing fresh market.

text.p: Swedish car safety equipment maker Autoliv AB said on Tuesday that the new company to be formed from the proposed merger with a unit of Morton International would have growth potential on new markets.
The new company, Autoliv Inc., will be created through the merger of Autoliv and the vehicle safety unit of Morton International Inc.
"There are several markets that look interesting where neither Autoliv nor Morton have their own production," former Autoliv managing director Gunnar Bark told Reuters.
"The markets I see with potential are South Korea -- where three million cars are manufactured annually -- Japan and Brazil," he said.
Bark, who is proposed to become chairman of the new group, emphasised organic growth as the main path to expansion.

"The highest priority is always organic growth, but I am not excluding continued acquisitions," Bark said. "The business will probably consist of just three to four companies when restructuring is over."
"The market will keep growing and it will take some years before it will be a mature sector."
Autoliv Inc. will focus on research and development, he said.

"I do not see a limit on the number of products which can be developed to improve car safety and the new company will keep focusing on research and development to the same degree as today," Bark said.
Bark proposed a merger with Morton two and a half years ago and he said he saw large advantages with it. He added that it would take time to overcome all obstacles.
"The merger will take long time and will mean several cultural shocks...You can see that when looking at similar previous mergers."
